brand.name: Las Cabrillas
brand.description: Not on the site at all - confirmed absent from the site's full brand index. Line named after New World explorers (Balboa, De Soto, Cortez, Columbus, Vasco De Gama). Uses an unusual-for-Honduras all-Mexican binder/filler tobacco (San Andres/Tuxtla Valley) while being rolled in Honduras - retailers describe this combination as rare. No source gives a founding date or founder; multiple retailers describe it only as a 'long-standing' brand with 'a loyal following dating back many years' and 'best seller for over two decades.' Two wrapper treatments exist brand-wide: Natural (Connecticut Shade) and Maduro (San Andres).
brand.founded_note: No founding date found - described only vaguely as long-standing (20+ years) by retailers.
brand.origin_country: Honduras (rolled); Mexico (binder and filler tobacco - San Andres/Tuxtla Valley)

line.name: Las Cabrillas Balboa
line.description: Medium-bodied; flavor notes of earth, black pepper, cocoa. FLAG: wrapper identity conflicts across sources (see wrapper field).
line.wrapper: San Andres (Mexico) per one retailer (Mike's Cigars spec); a JR Cigars blending-room article instead describes it as 'Connecticut Broadleaf maduro' for the same product - CONFLICT, not resolved.

vitolas.name: Maduro (Churchill shape)
vitolas.size: UNVERIFIED - no retailer lists exact length x ring gauge for the Maduro specifically. Matches the Mac photo, labeled 'Maduro.' The Natural version of this same vitola is confirmed at 7.5x54; a JR blending-room article calls the Maduro a 'medium-bodied Churchill' implying a similar size, but no page states the Maduro's dimensions directly.

research_notes: Only 'Balboa' (Natural, confirmed 7.5x54) and 'Balboa Maduro' (size unlisted) were found - no additional Balboa sub-sizes identified anywhere.
